row availability is the actual's availability; consensus_quality names the consensus provenance (exact only for consensus captured by our timer before the release, unvintaged otherwise)

exact: our own live capture, available_utc equals captured_utc; published: an agency vintage (ALFRED, FOMC statement) or provider actual/previous/revision whose availability is the scheduled release instant in available_utc, null when only the day (available_date) is known; unvintaged: a consensus read from a calendar after the event, available_utc set to the capture time, never before the release

Per-row clock_quality. published rows: available_utc is realtime_start + 1 day 00:00 UTC (available_rule next_day_00utc), or the series' first ALFRED vintage + 1 day for pre-tracking history (first_vintage_next_day_00utc; a lower bound, not a publication instant). unvintaged rows (available_rule vintage_precedes_observation): FRED's vintage date precedes the observation period, no credible availability instant, available_utc null.

Every row is published. available_utc = loaded_utc (Socrata :created_at, the row's API load instant, 15:30 ET on the actual publication day) when the row was loaded one report at a time, else release_utc (15:30 ET on the scheduled release day from the captured CFTC schedule pages or press release 7864-19); available_source says which. release_caveat marks report weeks whose scheduled day is documented as wrong or uncertain (2013 and 2018-19 lapses in appropriations, Juneteenth 2021, 2023 ION incident, 2025-01-09 day of mourning, 2025 lapse).

Every row is published: available_utc is FBIL's stated displayTime (published_ist, Asia/Kolkata) in UTC; we did not capture at that time. usdinr_dexinus is the latest FRED vintage joined on the civil date for cross-checking only and carries no clock.

The exchange publishes the Bhav Copy after the session closes and we did not capture it live, so every row is published with unknown latency. available_utc is the session's close instant from mcx_sessions (evening close 23:30 or 23:55 IST per the hours circular in force, the 17:00 morning close on morning-only days, the Muhurat or budget-session close where one applies); for a session whose evening close no retained circular states, the later published close (23:55 IST) is used so the instant is never earlier than the true close.

Each row's state and hours are stated by the circulars in evidence_ids; available_utc is 00:00 UTC of the day after the latest of their issue dates (the annual trading-holiday circular alone for ordinary and holiday dates it governs, plus the Revision in Trading Hours circular that states the evening close, plus any single-date circular such as an election closure, a Muhurat timing or a budget-day live session). Rows classed unvintaged assert the 23:30 fallback evening close past the last retained hours circular: their state is published at available_utc but their close time has no circular behind it.
created_at is the feed's own computation time: exact.
clock inherited from the cluster version's created_at (exact).

exact when fetched_at is within 24 h after published_at (the feed polled the source while the item was fresh); otherwise published, with available_utc = fetched_at, the first instant the feed had the item. published_utc is the publisher's label and never an availability clock.

TE rows (adapter te:*, status live): ts = datetime.now(UTC) when the shared TE cache was read (<= 10 s after the fetch), so exact and conservative. yfinance fallback rows: ts is the 1m bar time: published, available_utc = bar time.

Rows with contractEvidence.observedActiveContract.observedAt (from 2026-07-23): exact, fetched_utc = observedAt. Earlier rows: published, available_utc = regularMarketTime (Yahoo's delayed feed shows a trade roughly 10-15 minutes after it prints, so true availability is later than this bound).
ts is datetime.now(UTC) at the poll by the upstream collector: exact; available_utc = fetched_utc.

Rows without a transport key (2026-06-22..2026-07-14 polling era) have ts stamped by the feed at the poll: exact, available_utc = fetched_utc. Rows with transport angel_ws/angel_rest have ts = the exchange timestamp (Reading.ts), not a capture clock: published, available_utc = max(ts, exchFeedTime, exchTradeTime). Capture followed within the collector's freshness window for live rows (WS delivery; REST fetch - exchFeedTime <= 60 s) and with unbounded lag for delayed rows.

fetched_utc = raw linuxReceivedTs (feed receive clock), else raw fetchTs (bridge capture clock): exact. available_utc = fetched_utc (the bridge's own availabilityTs is a few hundred ms earlier and is not used as the pack clock). Rows with neither clock would be published on eventTs; none observed.

shfe/ine: ts = datetime.now(UTC) at the Sina poll: exact. lbma: ts = the auction time (gold 15:00, silver 12:00 London): published. goldapi: ts = provider updatedAt: published. investing: ts = the bar time of a delayed chart API: published. lme_westmetall: the source gives a date only (timestamp_precision = date): unvintaged; raw_file_date bounds availability from above.
ts is datetime.now(UTC) at the poll by the upstream collector: exact; available_utc = fetched_utc.
fetched_ts is the feed's own capture clock: exact. The CFTC release instant the feed recorded is kept as release_utc.

A swing row's availability is the settlement publication of the session its extreme printed in: that session's close instant from mcx_sessions, the same convention mcx_daily uses. The exchange publishes at or after the close and we did not capture at that instant, so the class is published. confirm_available_utc is the same published clock read on the session of the bar that completed the leg, and it is the column a point-in-time consumer must use; it is not named under clocks because that mapping holds one column per class and available_utc is the file's primary availability column. The bar instants are not availability: an hourly bar carries the quotes' own clocks (mcx_quotes states exact or published per row) and a daily bar carries the session's opening instant, inside which the Bhav Copy high and low printed at an unknown time, and confirm_utc is a bar instant of that kind.
